newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: INTERVIEW - S.Africa's Stals stays wary after data.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - S.Africa's Stals stays wary after data.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Wednesday he remained extremely cautious of any change in monetary policy following the release of three keenly-awaited economic indicators.

Figures for consumer price inflation showed the annual rate climbed to a 22-month high of 9.9 percent in April, up from 9.6 percent in March and higher than the consensus forecast for an unchanged rate of 9.6 again.

Stals said the figure was disappointing but that April was always going to be something of an anomaly since the year-ago base comparison was low and the effects of the rand's depreciation had still not shown through fully.
"It is worrying that it is still going up but the April figure can be explained partly by technical factors," he said.
"From May onwards we begin to compare prices after depreciation with prices after depreciation. It will very important for us how these statistics develop in the next month, in May."
Economists have speculated that the April inflation figure would mark the peak of the present cycle, but Stals said it was too early to say if this was the case.
On money supply, Stals said there was little clear evidence of a change in trend with money supply growth around 15 percent and credit extension climbing again.
The Reserve Bank's guideline range for M3 growth is six to 10 percent.

South Africa's year-on-year broadly defined M3 money supply grew 15.44 percent in April from a revised to 16.46 percent in March. Annual private sector credit growth was 16.95 percent against 15.95 percent in March.
A Reuters consensus poll of economists had forecast M3 year-on-year growth of 16.70 percent while private credit was seen expanding 16.40 percent.
